documents.abstract: Ambulatory surgery and the concept of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) are deeply integrated, reshaping the surgical care model. This article systematically reviews and critically analyzes advances in ERAS-driven ambulatory surgery across multiple dimensions, including its current status, the expanding scope of enhanced recovery, and future perspectives. Available evidence shows that ERAS-guided ambulatory surgery not only ensures surgical safety but also significantly shortens hospital stay, reduces medical costs, and improves patient satisfaction. In the future, technologies such as artificial intelligence, wearable devices, and telemonitoring will further promote ambulatory surgery toward individualization, comfort, and intelligence.

Pediatric anesthesia in China currently faces challenges including shortages of qualified personnel and a low degree of specialization, which seriously affect perioperative safety in children. Drawing on recent evidence, this article focuses on three major issues: emergence delirium, airway management safety, and perioperative pain management. Specifically, we discuss individualizing medication and detecting burst suppression guided by electroencephalographic monitoring to reduce the risk of emergence delirium; optimizing airway safety through risk stratification, appropriate selection of airway devices, and anesthesia maintenance strategies; and implementing opioid-sparing anesthesia centered on regional anesthesia and multimodal analgesia. Furthermore, we emphasize the necessity of personnel training, quality control, and artificial intelligence-assisted decision support to drive a paradigm shift from an experience-based to a data-driven practice, which is essential to ensuring pediatric safety from the beginning of life.

Abstract This article asks what it means, from a Christian philosophical perspective, to say that artificial intelligence can mediate human speech but cannot possess voice. Language-generating systems and translation systems produce outputs that recipients use within religious, journalistic, and educational practices. The article distinguishes communicative uptake from voice, authorship, and responsible agency. Voice is not a property of output but the embodied, relational, and morally answerable act of a person; authorship names how a human or institution appropriates and answers for a text. While AI may extend, translate, and summarize human speech, it cannot supply its own accountability. Drawing on Reformational philosophy and Vatican materials, the article treats AI-assisted liturgical translation as a limit case, distinguishing translation and summarization from open-ended generation, whose outputs lack testimonial authority unless independently verified and responsibly adopted. It concludes with five criteria for Christian communication: accountability, transparency, dignity, embodied voice, and attention to linguistic inequality.

documents.abstract: Background: The Virage project collected approximately 800 one-hour interviews on rabies awareness, including transmission, disease progression, and vaccination. Manually searching, comparing, and coding this corpus would require substantial time and human resources. Objective: EpiChat and EpiCode were developed using large language models (LLMs) to support natural-language interrogation and thematic analysis of interview transcripts. Local LLMs were used to preserve data privacy, avoid sharing data with foreign cloud services, and eliminate token and subscription costs. Methods: EpiChat uses an LLM-based router to direct questions to three specialized pipelines. An SQL pipeline translates structured metadata questions into database queries. For questions regarding counts or proportions, a map-reduce pipeline examines each interview independently and aggregates the results. Explanatory questions are handled using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Because conventional RAG retrieves only the highest-ranked passages across the corpus, it may overlook rare perspectives that are important to qualitative research. To address this, EpiChat introduces a deep search mode that formulates the question as a quotation and searches for it into each interview. Verified quotations from matching interviews are then combined into a single response with source citations. EpiCode supports qualitative coding by matching transcript segments to a two-level codebook of main codes and subcodes. Each suggested code includes a model-generated confidence score, supporting quotation, and brief rationale. When no existing code adequately represents the content, the system proposes a new code. All suggestions require researcher review and approval. Results: Preliminary runtime measurements showed that EpiChat processed an interview-level query in approximately four seconds per interview, while EpiCode generated code suggestions for an entire interview in around three minutes. Conclusion: EpiChat and EpiCode provide a privacy-preserving, locally deployed platform for AI-assisted qualitative analysis. Future work will compare AI-generated codebooks with human-developed codebooks and evaluate whether EpiChat produces answers consistent with findings derived from manual coding. Poster presented at the Pasteur Network Annual Meeting (PNAM 2026), Laval, Canada, 3–5 November 2026.

Abstract The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven their growing adoption across domains, including healthcare. However, these models risk amplifying existing healthcare disparities. This systematic review synthesizes the existing literature on bias assessment in LLMs applied within the healthcare domain. We searched six databases, namely, Scopus, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library, for studies published between January 2020 and May 2025, with the final search conducted on 16 May 2025. Retrieved records were screened according to predefined criteria, resulting in 74 included articles. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. Owing to methodological heterogeneity, findings were described narratively. LLMs were applied across various healthcare contexts, most notably in medical question answering. Bias assessment methods ranged from human evaluations to statistical analyses, while only 13.5% of the included studies implemented mitigation strategies, which were primarily prompt-based. Overall, 87.8% of the studies reported evidence of bias, with demographic bias being the most commonly investigated bias type. The included studies were of predominantly high quality with minimal risk of bias. The findings indicate that bias remains prevalent in LLM healthcare outputs, highlighting a critical challenge to their equitable and responsible deployment. Future studies should prioritize robust bias evaluation and the implementation of effective bias mitigation strategies to support the safe integration of LLMs into healthcare.

documents.abstract: Background: Single-cell RNA-seq has transformed biological research by resolving cellular heterogeneity invisible to bulk approaches, revealing fine cell types, elucidating host responses to infection, vaccination, and disease. Objectives: Hierarchical annotation models mirror the hierarchical definition of cell types, but existing tools fix a single classifier family and often feature space across all nodes. We offer a flexible hierarchical cell type annotation framework with a unified interface, supporting several classification methods, user-defined cell-types, node-specific feature selection and classifiers, and pre-trained human PMBC models. Methods: Hereby we introduce CATNAP, a customizable hierarchical cell-type annotation framework. It is fully modular: catnap_core drives the cell type annotation, given a cell type hierarchy tree, specifying which classifier and parameters shall be used for each subtree. Cell type hierarchies, model parameter presets and other configuration files, tailored to human PMBC studies, are available in catnap_preset. New models can be trained with own data or curated bundles of publicly available datasets, using catnap_pretrain. Finally, catnap_evaluation defines standardized metrics and representations for model performance assessment and comparisons among sets of models. Any classifier can be integrated, registering new catnap_core backends. We provide backends for predictors spanning correlation-based (Spearman), distance-based (k-nearest neighbors, nearest mean centroid), classical machine learning (logistic regression, random forest, gradient tree boosting, support vector machine), probabilistic (linear discriminant analysis, scANVI) and foundation models (Geneformer). Results: CATNAP was used for training, and cell-types prediction on six human PBMC scRNA-seq datasets. A scANVI-based hierarchical model achieved 86.42% accuracy and 83.61% macro-F1 on these datasets, and 55.31% accuracy and 51.38% macro-F1 on two additional out-of-distribution datasets. Conclusions: CATNAP is a customizable hierarchical cell-type annotation framework, providing also a framework for benchmarking existing methods, and a prototyping environment for new classifiers. Future work will explore model combinations, and alternative configurations for exploiting the full potential of our customizable hierarchical framework. Poster presented at the Pasteur Network Annual Meeting (PNAM 2026), Laval, Canada, 3–5 November 2026.

The integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly altered academic writing practices in higher education, yet its pedagogical implications for pre-service English teachers remain underexplored. This qualitative case study aimed to investigate English Education students' perceptions of utilizing AI tools in academic writing, specifically examining perceived benefits, operational challenges, and academic integrity negotiations. Ten undergraduate students, comprising eight eighth-semester and two sixth-semester students at Institut Pendidikan Indonesia, were purposively recruited. Data were gathered through an asynchronous online open-ended questionnaire and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis framework. The findings revealed that students utilized AI tools primarily for brainstorming, outlining, and grammatical refinement, while contending with fabricated citations, stylistic rigidity, and anxieties regarding the erosion of independent critical thinking. In negotiating academic integrity, participants practiced selective verification and established a collective ethical boundary that endorsed linguistic scaffolding while strictly proscribing unreflective wholesale text generation. ABSTRAK Integrasi kecerdasan buatan generatif (generative artificial intelligence) telah merevolusi praktik penulisan akademik di perguruan tinggi, namun pemaknaan pedagogis oleh mahasiswa calon guru bahasa Inggris masih jarang diteliti secara mendalam. Penelitian studi kasus kualitatif ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi persepsi mahasiswa Pendidikan Bahasa Inggris terhadap penggunaan perangkat kecerdasan buatan (AI tools) dalam penulisan akademik, yang berfokus pada persepsi manfaat, tantangan, dan negosiasi integritas akademik. Sebanyak sepuluh mahasiswa sarjana yang terdiri atas delapan mahasiswa Semester 8 dan dua mahasiswa Semester 6 di Institut Pendidikan Indonesia dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dihimpun melalui kuesioner terbuka daring asinkron (asynchronous open-ended questionnaire) dan dianalisis menggunakan analisis tematik enam tahap. Hasil penelitian mengungkapkan bahwa mahasiswa memanfaatkan perangkat kecerdasan buatan terutama untuk pencarian ide awal, penyusunan kerangka karangan, serta perbaikan tata bahasa, meskipun mereka menghadapi kendala berupa sitasi halusinasi, kekakuan gaya bahasa, dan kecemasan akan erosi keterampilan berpikir kritis mandiri. Dalam menegosiasikan integritas akademik, mahasiswa menerapkan adopsi selektif dengan memverifikasi rujukan ilmiah serta menyepakati batasan etis bahwa bantuan penyuntingan bahasa dapat dibenarkan, sedangkan penyalinan teks secara utuh merupakan bentuk pelanggaran.

This study aims to explore English teachers’ perceptions regarding the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in teaching writing at the senior high school level. A qualitative descriptive case study design was employed at a public senior high school in Garut, West Java. The participants were two experienced English teachers purposively selected based on their teaching tenure and digital tool integration. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews, pedagogical document analysis, and observational field notes, then examined using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis. The analysis yielded six core themes: GenAI as a support for student writing, GenAI as a support for teaching, GenAI as a risk to independent learning, GenAI as a risk to textual authenticity, GenAI as a tool demanding responsible use, and GenAI as a challenge for writing assessment. The findings demonstrate that teachers maintain a conditional and context-dependent perception of AI integration. While teachers recognize its utility for lexical scaffolding and conceptual brainstorming, they emphasize rigorous boundary setting to prevent the erosion of learner autonomy and textual originality. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi persepsi guru bahasa Inggris terhadap pemanfaatan Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) dalam pembelajaran menulis pada jenjang sekolah menengah atas. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus deskriptif pada sebuah SMA negeri di Garut, Jawa Barat. Partisipan terdiri atas dua orang guru bahasa Inggris berpengalaman yang dipilih secara purposif berdasarkan kriteria masa kerja dan kebiasaan memanfaatkan teknologi digital. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, analisis artefak pembelajaran, dan catatan lapangan, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan analisis tematik model enam tahap Braun dan Clarke. Hasil analisis menghasilkan enam tema utama: GenAI sebagai pendukung tulisan siswa, GenAI sebagai pendukung pengajaran, GenAI sebagai risiko terhadap pembelajaran mandiri siswa, GenAI sebagai risiko terhadap keaslian tulisan, GenAI sebagai alat yang memerlukan penggunaan bertanggung jawab, dan GenAI sebagai tantangan bagi asesmen menulis. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa persepsi guru bersifat kondisional dan terikat pada konteks pedagogis di ruang kelas. Guru memandang GenAI bermanfaat untuk stimulasi kosakata dan ide awal, namun penggunaannya harus dibatasi agar tidak mengikis kemandirian berpikir serta orisinalitas karya tulis siswa.

Educational assessment at the elementary level extends beyond measuring the extent to which instructional objectives have been achieved, as it also influences students’ perceptions of their own abilities, the quality of classroom participation, and their motivation to continue learning. The present article aims to explain the role of modern assessment models in enhancing learning motivation among elementary school students and to identify the psychological and educational mechanisms underlying this relationship. This study employs a descriptive-analytical approach based on library research and a review of relevant scholarly articles. The analysis examines the characteristics of descriptive assessment, formative assessment, performance-based assessment, self-assessment, peer assessment, and portfolio assessment, with particular emphasis on constructive feedback, active participation, and attention to individual progress. Findings derived from the reviewed literature indicate that replacing exclusively grade-centered judgment with clear and process-oriented feedback can strengthen students’ sense of competence, academic self-efficacy, responsibility, and intrinsic motivation. Furthermore, opportunities to correct errors, awareness of one’s progress, and reduced pressure resulting from comparisons among students can promote more informed and active participation in learning activities. The effectiveness of these assessment models depends on teachers’ ability to establish clear criteria, accommodate individual differences, and involve families in the educational process. Accordingly, modern assessment can become a source of motivation when it is integrated continuously into the teaching process, thereby making the learning experience more meaningful.

This working paper investigates how supplier research can distinguish evidence age, source lineage and decision scope. It combines a purposive literature and standards synthesis with three separate Python demonstrations using constructed fixtures. A scope regression shows that selecting the latest assertion by field and source alone can discard a different supplier or service; partitioning by entity and scope before historical selection prevents that specific loss. The modules passed 14, 13 and 10 separate assertions, not an integrated accuracy evaluation. Scope identifiers and lineage are manually supplied. No production qualification, customer outcome or empirical supplier accuracy is established. Mohammad Maani established the research direction, supervised the work, supplied methodological decisions and an explicitly author-reported shipping illustration, reviewed and accepted the scope-isolation interpretation and figure, and authorized publication. Independent human code replication or source-by-source verification is not asserted. OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted research, synthesis, drafting, code and synthetic-test design and execution; OpenAI image generation produced the conceptual artwork. AI is not an author. This deposit is not peer reviewed. The author is Founder of QuickAIBuy and has a commercial interest in its development. Project: https://www.quickaibuy.com . Version 1.0 includes the manuscript and reproducibility materials. CC BY 4.0 applies to the manuscript, original diagram and synthetic materials; trademark and font-license exceptions are documented.

Financial Management courses often fall short in linking computational training with financing decision analysis. Taking finance leasing as a case, this paper explores how generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) can be brought into the classroom. The instructional design is built around a scenario in which a private hospital finances the purchase of medical equipment, and it connects rent calculation, comparison of financing alternatives, and scrutiny of decision conditions through a four-stage process: independent calculation, AI questioning, professional verification, and decision reconstruction. Students first carry out the calculations and form a preliminary financing judgment, then use generative AI to interrogate financing constraints and uncover the assumptions behind a plan, and finally verify the AI-generated content against financial principles to strengthen their argument. The design takes students' own judgments as the starting point of human-AI interaction and assigns AI the role of revealing and examining the conditions under which a financing plan holds, rather than making the decision for them. This approach offers a reference for bringing generative AI into accounting and finance courses.

Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as patient-facing informational tools in dentistry, but their suitability for postoperative communication in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMFS) remains uncertain. This study compared ChatGPT-5.4 Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2, and Gemini 3 (Thinking mode) in answering routine postoperative OMFS questions. Methods Thirty standardised open-ended postoperative questions were submitted once to each model through public web interfaces using the same neutral prompt. Three OMFS surgeons, masked to model identity, independently rated overall informational quality using an adapted 5-point Global Quality Score (GQS). Factual accuracy, completeness, and clinical safety were rated against a question-specific Reference Answer and Safety Framework; all responses were reassessed after peer review, and both rating sets were analysed. Five readability indices and user-interface latency were recorded. Friedman tests with Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon post hoc tests were used. Results GQS inter-rater reliability was excellent [ICC(2,1), 0.900–0.926]. Mean GQS differed across models ( p < 0.001): Gemini 3 (Thinking mode) 4.82 ± 0.38, DeepSeek-V3.2 4.53 ± 0.49, and ChatGPT-5.4 Thinking 4.08 ± 0.64. Original accuracy and completeness ratings showed limited agreement [ICC(2,1), 0.379 and 0.272]. Factual accuracy differed in the original ratings ( p = 0.014) but not after reassessment ( p = 0.115); completeness did not differ. Of 90 responses, 89 were classified as Safe; one Gemini response on clopidogrel resumption was classified as Missed Red Flag/False Reassurance. After adjustment for word count, Gemini retained higher GQS than both other models (both p < 0.001). Gemini responses were generally more linguistically complex. Observed latency was shortest for DeepSeek-V3.2 (10.49 ± 1.95 s) and longest for Gemini (31.46 ± 11.60 s) and does not represent intrinsic model speed. Conclusions Gemini 3 (Thinking mode) achieved the highest expert-rated informational quality, but between-model differences in factual accuracy were not robust to reassessment, completeness did not differ, and one clinically consequential safety concern was identified. The findings are limited to simulated, single-turn, English-language first responses and do not establish patient comprehension or real-world safety. LLM-generated postoperative information should remain under professional oversight.

documents.abstract: The increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into higher education has created new opportunities to support the learning process. However, the effectiveness of technology utilization is not solely determined by technical availability, but also by students' active involvement in learning activities. This study aims to analyze the role of AI utilization and digital infrastructure in enhancing learning effectiveness, with student engagement serving as a mediating variable among students at Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. A quantitative survey approach was administered to 347 active students across faculties and cohorts selected through multistage stratified sampling. Data were gathered using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with a second-order construct through the Hierarchical Component Model. The results demonstrate that AI usage and digital infrastructure exert positive and significant effects on student engagement and learning effectiveness. Furthermore, student engagement partially mediates the effects of AI usage and digital infrastructure on learning effectiveness, with AI usage exhibiting a more dominant total contribution. ABSTRAK Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan teknologi digital telah memberikan peluang baru dalam mendukung proses pembelajaran di perguruan tinggi. Namun, efektivitas pemanfaatan teknologi tidak hanya ditentukan oleh ketersediaan fasilitas semata, melainkan juga oleh keterlibatan aktif mahasiswa dalam proses akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran pemanfaatan AI dan infrastruktur digital dalam meningkatkan efektivitas belajar dengan keterlibatan mahasiswa (student engagement) sebagai variabel mediasi pada mahasiswa Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei diterapkan kepada 347 mahasiswa aktif dari berbagai fakultas dan angkatan yang dipilih melalui teknik multistage stratified sampling. Pengumpulan data menggunakan kuesioner skala Likert lima tingkat dan dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan model konstruk tingkat kedua melalui Hierarchical Component Model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan AI dan infrastruktur digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keterlibatan mahasiswa serta efektivitas belajar. Selain itu, keterlibatan mahasiswa terbukti memediasi secara parsial pengaruh penggunaan AI dan infrastruktur digital terhadap efektivitas belajar, dengan pemanfaatan AI memberikan kontribusi total yang lebih dominan.

Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is now present in every stage of the academic research life cycle, yet the rules governing its use remain fragmented. Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review used 34 structured search strings and citation chasing to search literature published between 2015 and 2025. Of 359 records identified, 124 studies and documents met the inclusion criteria: 40 empirical studies, 43 conceptual analyses or commentaries, 20 policy and guidance documents, 17 reviews and 4 methodological frameworks; 83% were published from 2023 onwards. Guidance converges on a narrow set of standards: AI cannot be an author, material use must be disclosed, and humans remain accountable. Disclosure thresholds, AI in peer review, AI-generated images, AI-text detectors and the regulatory treatment of research remain contested. Challenges fall into three clusters: algorithmic bias; data governance, privacy and consent; and transparency, reproducibility and integrity, where empirical studies document fabricated references, unreliable and biased detectors, and rapidly rising, mostly undisclosed AI use. Emerging responses include lifecycle-based guidance, structured documentation, tailored ethics review and interdisciplinary oversight. We propose an integrated framework linking five principles to five research stages and an agenda emphasizing context-sensitive ethics, public participation and international coordination.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for first-pass resume screening, yet the resume is supplied by the party who benefits from a favourable outcome. Applicants can therefore conceal text from human reviewers (white or microscopic fonts, zero-width characters, homoglyphs) or embed instructions that steer the model . We present SecureResume, a layered framework that (i) parses documents in a render-aware manner and removes concealed or instruction-like content, (ii) scores per-object adversarial risk with an Isolation Forest, (iii) computes Sentence-BERT job–resume similarity, and (iv) forces an LLM to emit schema-validated claims that are verified against evidence in the sanitised text, producing an evidence-adjusted ranking score. We implement the system as a FastAPI/Next.js application and evaluate its security-aware parsing layer on a controlled benchmark of 400 synthetic PDF resumes covering nine concealment techniques. After fixing two defects we found in our own parser, the rule-based layer detects all seven concealment classes it targets (280/280) with no false positives on 40 clean resumes, but misses off-page and low-contrast text; the document-level risk score, as originally formulated, saturates and is not discriminative . We report these findings candidly and outline calibration and rendering-based extensions. The LLM verification stages are specified but not yet evaluated.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract Segmentation is a major bottleneck in three-dimensional morphological analysis. Although artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation workflows can be used to address this issue, their implementations are constrained by dedicated software environments or local computing resources. To address these challenges, we developed SegRef3D Lite, a browser-based platform that integrates two complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation approaches (namely, SegAnything and SegCT/MRI) within a common human-in-the-loop workflow. SegAnything provides general-purpose, prompt-based segmentation by using Segment Anything Model 2, and SegCT/MRI provides anatomy-specific segmentations of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging datasets by using TotalSegmentator. Both approaches generate segmentation masks that can be imported into the same browser-based workspace for visual review, manual correction, quantitative volume measurement, three-dimensional visualization, and surface-model export. In this workspace, routine image handling and refinement are performed locally in the browser, whereas artificial intelligence inference is executed through user-initiated Google Colaboratory workflows, thus eliminating the need for a compatible graphics processing unit on a local computer. We applied our platform to serial block-face photographs, volumetric computed tomography, serial light microscopy, serial electron microscopy, and human abdominal computed tomography. Across these diverse imaging modalities and spatial scales, our platform is able to process outputs from different segmentation approaches by using the same downstream workflow for review, refinement, quantitative analysis, and three-dimensional reconstruction. Therefore, SegRef3D Lite provides an accessible framework for integrating complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation strategies with researcher-guided verification and quantitative morphological analysis. Mini-abstract : SegRef3D Lite integrates general-purpose and anatomy-specific artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation with browser-based human refinement, volume measurement, and three-dimensional reconstruction across diverse morphological imaging modalities.

This paper describes a leaf classification framework based on machine learning methodologies. The dataset included 36 leaf species with 340 instances and 16 features. Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, AdaBoost, and Random Forest were applied initially on the raw dataset. It was found that Decision Tree, XGBoost and Random Forest performed well, with accuracy scores of 53%, 60% and 85% respectively. After feature reduction based on Information Gain and correlation matrix analysis, four highly correlated features were removed. This led to a marginal improvement in accuracy to 60% for Decision Tree and to 65% percentage for XG Boost, while the accuracy of Random Forest dropped to 74%. We also applied SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique) to balance the raw dataset. This enhanced the accuracy of Random Forest and XGBoost to 91% and 81% respectively. With Computer Vision, we achieved an accuracy of 66% for SVM, 61% for Random Forest, 43% for K-NN and 37% for the Decision Tree classifier on the image dataset. The pre-trained VGG16 model achieved an impressive 90.47% accuracy, outperforming the custom CNN model and conventional models like Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and KNN with various K-values from the literature

Abstract Trust in artificial intelligence clinical decision support systems is critical to appropriate reliance, yet its measurement and behavioral implications remain unclear. We conducted a scoping review of quantitative studies published between January 2010 and June 2026, searching PubMed, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase. Thirty-three studies met inclusion criteria. Fourteen (42.4%) explicitly defined trust, and 16 (48.5%) assessed anticipated or hypothetical trust without direct system interaction. Twenty-seven studies (81.8%) examined factors associated with trust, emphasizing human–AI interaction and system characteristics over organizational and social contexts. Trust patterns varied across healthcare professionals, patients, and general populations, although direct comparisons were rare. Twenty-seven studies assessed separate AI-related behavioral outcomes, but only 11 formally tested trust–behavior relationships. Reported trust did not consistently correspond to preferences or decisions when AI and clinician recommendations conflicted. More comparable measures and observed behavioral outcomes are needed to evaluate appropriately calibrated trust in clinical AI.

documents.abstract: This workshop shares the experience of building a deep phenotyping dataset of music-evoked emotions, namely "ManyMusic🎶" (). This ongoing project involves 17 EEG sessions and 17 fMRI sessions per participant, measuring neural and behavioural responses during intense affective experiences evoked by complete musical works spanning a wide range of genres, including Western classical, jazz, rock, pop, hip-hop, and more. Across six participants, the project will collect data from more than 1,000 full-length musical pieces.In this workshop, we will discuss the challenges of building a deep phenotyping dataset such as stimulus selection, participant screening, data quality monitoring, and on-the-fly troubleshooting. Participants will also have the opportunity to examine a subset of the collected EEG data first-hand. We will conclude by discussing the future prospects of developing foundation models from deeply sampled multimodal datasets.

The Internet of Things (IoT) links sensors, machines, vehicles and everyday objects so that they can exchange data and act with little human intervention. Fifth-generation (5G) networks introduced dedicated support for massive machine-type and ultra-reliable low-latency communication, but emerging applications such as autonomous transport, remote surgery, immersive extended reality and large-scale digital twins demand still higher data rates, lower latency, greater reliability, precise positioning and far denser connectivity. Sixth-generation (6G) networks, now being defined under the IMT-2030 framework, aim to meet these needs and to make artificial intelligence a native part of the network. This survey reviews 6G-enabled IoT. It summarises the requirements and key performance indicators, and explains the enabling technologies: terahertz and sub-terahertz communication, intelligent reflecting surfaces, integrated sensing and communication, edge intelligence, AI-native network management and non-terrestrial networks. A five-layer architecture for 6G-enabled IoT is presented, linking devices, access, edge, core and applications under a cross-layer security and energy plane. Applications in smart cities, connected vehicles, healthcare, industrial automation, precision agriculture and environmental monitoring are discussed. Finally, open challenges including infrastructure cost, spectrum regulation, energy consumption, security and privacy, and the management of billions of devices are identified.

In computer vision, object detection and recognition processes are used to identify and locate objects in images. Humans can recognize a wide range of things in photos with little effort, even if the images vary somewhat from different angles, sizes, and scales, or when they are moved or rotated. Objects can be identified even when partially blocked from vision. This task remains a challenge for computer vision systems. Several approaches to the task have been implemented over the years. In many computer vision systems, the first duty is object detection, which allows us to learn more about the identified object and the scene. Researchers have recently focused their emphasis on the application of Machine learning techniques. Machine learning uses multiple layers to separate raw information into higher-level features. This paper outlines a recommended research methodology. This method uses a convolutional neural network-based architecture with a limited amount of data to detect objects in an image. The data used is the MAR database, and the process classifies thirty images into four distinct classes with high accuracy. The approaches outlined in this research included data collection and pre-processing, as well as designing and developing a hardwarebased machine learning system. This study discusses the many techniques to object identification, their similarities, the limitations of existing work, and, finally, the model given in the last section of the paper.

documents.abstract: Background Children with Down syndrome (DS) often experience delays in gross motor development due to hypotonia and motor coordination deficits, which can limit their participation in physical activities. Traditional assessments of motor performance are mainly subjective and may lack consistency across evaluators. Integrating artificial intelligence and computer vision into educational settings presents an opportunity to enhance the objectivity, precision, and scalability of such assessments. This study presents the development and evaluation of an automated system that utilizes pose estimation and machine learning to classify gross motor performance in children with Down syndrome, to support inclusive physical education practices. Methods We recruited 23 children with DS (aged 4–10) from educational institutions affiliated with Cáritas Arequipa, Peru. Participants performed four standardized gross motor exercises: two-footed jumps, ball toss, crawling, and sit-to-stand transitions. High-resolution Canon cameras recorded the movements, and the MediaPipe Holistic framework was used to extract 33 key body landmarks per frame. From these data, spatiotemporal features were computed and reduced using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to minimize dimensionality while preserving variance. Expert evaluators labeled each exercise attempt into one of three performance categories: high, moderate, or low. Five supervised machine learning algorithms—Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), and Logistic Regression—were trained and compared using a stratified 80/20 train-test split. Model performance was evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, accuracy, and Cohen’s Kappa coefficient. Results All classifiers achieved high accuracy (>93%). The Random Forest model yielded the most balanced and robust results, with an overall accuracy of 95.55%, macro-average F1-score of 0.96, and a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.933, indicating near-perfect agreement with expert labels. Logistic Regression showed slightly higher accuracy (95.79%) but was less effective at modeling nonlinear patterns. Notably, a one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) on the first principal component (PC1) revealed significant differences between performance classes (F(2, 9,123) = 62.98, p = 7.00 × 10 −28 , η² = 0.0143), confirming PC1 as a discriminative metric for motor performance. Misclassifications occurred primarily between adjacent categories ( e.g ., moderate vs . high), with minimal confusion between high and low classes. Conclusions The proposed system demonstrates strong potential as an objective and scalable solution for monitoring gross motor skills in children with DS using low-cost hardware and open-source tools. Its integration into educational settings may help personalize instruction and support inclusive physical education by providing real-time, data-informed feedback to educators.
topics: Down syndrome and intellectual disability research

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates access to information in education, increasing the importance of critically evaluating claims and their underlying assumptions. This study examined Grade 10 students’ ability to distinguish facts, opinions, and values in AI-related information at SMA Don Bosco Padang from a philosophy of science perspective. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed involving 33 students. Data were collected through a 15-item written test comprising five items each for fact, opinion, and value identification. Descriptive analysis examined frequencies, percentages of correct responses, score distributions, and classification error patterns. Across 495 responses, 337 were correct and 158 were incorrect, yielding an overall accuracy of 68.08%. Accuracy was highest for opinion identification (76.36%), followed by fact identification (67.88%) and value identification (60.00%). Value identification presented the greatest difficulty, with an error rate of 40.00%. These findings reveal descriptive differences in students’ classification performance, particularly their greater difficulty recognizing values within AI-related information. From a philosophy of science perspective, the results underscore the relevance of epistemology for evaluating evidence and the justification of claims, alongside axiology for recognizing ethical considerations. The study provides contextual evidence to inform AI literacy instruction that integrates information verification, critical reasoning, and ethical reflection to support responsible technology use.

Explainable machine learning has been applied to textual predictors of writing quality, but rarely to the behavioral and motivational predictors, feedback modality and self-regulated learning (SRL), that dominate confirmatory EFL writing research. This study analyzes a quasi-experimental, ten-week EFL writing-feedback intervention (n=84), recording feedback condition (instructor-mediated, automated, or generative-AI), proficiency, and 35-item SRL strategy use alongside pre/post analytic writing scores across six outcomes. A pre-modeling reliability check found the SRL questionnaire did not reproduce its published factor structure (Cronbach's alpha = 0.279), so a single composite served as the motivational predictor, with centered feedback-by-SRL interaction terms. Five model classes were compared under nested cross-validation with per-trait tuning. Random forest achieved the best aggregate performance (MCRMSE = 2.240, mean R² = 0.293); a stacked ensemble performed worse than its base learners on every trait (mean R² = −0.344). A fixed-hyperparameter baseline outperformed the nested-CV-tuned pipeline (MCRMSE 2.197 vs. 2.258), showing tuning, not feature engineering, degraded performance here. SHAP attribution identified feedback condition, especially generative-AI feedback, as the dominant predictor for all six outcomes, with feedback-by-SRL interactions outweighing SRL's own main effect on three of six traits. A multi-task neural network outperformed an equivalent single-task ensemble on every trait using 5.75 times fewer parameters. These results show explainable, cross-validated machine learning can corroborate confirmatory EFL writing findings while surfacing measurement and methodological cautions.

Ergonomic workstation design is essential for improving the fit between workers, tasks, and the work environment while reducing the risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders. The Ovako Working Posture Analysis System (OWAS) is widely used for ergonomic risk assessment; however, its conventional application to dynamic work can be inefficient because numerous working postures must be observed and evaluated. Moreover, conventional ergonomic design often requires multiple physical mock-ups, while motion-capture technologies such as Kinect are generally applied to existing work conditions, limiting their use for preventive evaluation during the design stage. This study proposes a digital ergonomics framework integrating workstation modeling, work-process simulation, and OWAS-based risk assessment for preventive ergonomic optimization. Digital models of the workstation and work activities were developed to simulate worker postures and identify potentially hazardous conditions before physical implementation. OWAS was used to classify postural risks and determine the required corrective actions. Workstation configurations and work procedures associated with higher risk levels were iteratively modified and reassessed in the digital environment. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can identify and reduce ergonomic risks during the design stage without extensive physical prototyping. Higher-risk postures were mitigated through iterative modifications of workstation configurations and work procedures. This framework provides a systematic preventive approach for integrating ergonomic assessment into workstation and work-process design, supporting safer working conditions while improving the efficiency of the ergonomic design process
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This study develops an extended Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) model that integrates innovation, artificial intelligence (AI), and digital transformation into a macroeconomic framework for Vietnam. The model employs a parsimonious, single-channel architecture: three forms of rival capital (physical, digital, and AI) enter a single production function, while a non-rival knowledge stock drives endogenous total factor productivity. Calibrated using Vietnamese aggregate evidence and policy anchors for 2000–2024, supplemented by international proxy ranges, the model shows that sustained, institutionally supported investment in AI and digital transformation can raise long-run output and welfare. The magnitude of these conditional gains is moderate and depends strongly on institutional quality and public spending, while remaining quantitatively sensitive to selected knowledge and policy parameters. Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation offer opportunities to improve productivity and living standards in Vietnam. Using an economic model calibrated to Vietnamese macroeconomic evidence for 2000–2024, this study explores alternative investment scenarios. The simulations suggest that sustained investment can raise output and aggregate welfare, with gains depending on institutional capacity to convert public spending into productive knowledge. For policymakers, the implications are to strengthen project selection, accountable implementation, data governance and workforce skills alongside investment, and to phase expenditure according to implementation capacity. Reskilling and support for affected workers matter because aggregate gains do not ensure equal benefits across groups. These are conditional simulations using calibrated AI and digital capital stocks, not forecasts or direct estimates of realised economic effects. The framework can inform policy appraisal and public debate on how technology investment and institutional reform can jointly support Vietnam’s long-term development.

Geospatial technology is a combination of the Global Positioning System (GPS), remote sensing, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). It is an emerging technology used to capture, analyze, and visualize geographical data, also known as spatial data. This technology has undergone a transformation from traditional cartography and paper maps to smart, intelligent systems for mapping. This smart, artificial intelligence (AI)-based mapping system (AI GIS) has redefined data acquisition, spatial processing, and visualization. This chapter presents a detailed overview of geospatial technology, the emergence of digital mapping from paper maps, smart maps, the evolution from static maps to GIS, remote sensing platforms, Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), and Web GIS infrastructures. Later, this chapter also discusses various real-time applications, such as disaster management, traffic management, weather forecasting, and advanced technological developments such as cloud computing, the Internet of Things, digital twins, machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, natural language processing, and spatial statistics. Object detection and tracking methods further improve the observation of spatial data from satellite imagery. Furthermore, a four-layer AI GIS architecture model is discussed. Finally, key research challenges and future technological directions are presented.

Abstract Just-in-Time (JIT) software defect prediction tries to flag risky commits the moment they are committed, before they can cause problems in a codebase. Most existing approaches rely on simple change metrics, such as how many lines were added or how experienced the developer is, but these numbers say very little about what a change actually does. This paper presents a hybrid framework that looks at a commit from three angles at once: traditional change metrics, a semantic understanding of the code from CodeBERT, and structured reasoning about intent and risk generated by a large language model. We built a multi-language dataset of nearly 60,000 commits from 19 open-source Java, Python, and C/C++ projects, and tested several ways of combining these three sources of information using standard machine learning classifiers. Combining traditional metrics with CodeBERT's code understanding consistently gave the strongest results, clearly outperforming any single source used alone. Adding the LLM-based reasoning on top of that combination did not meaningfully improve things further, though it was genuinely useful when paired with either of the other two sources on its own. Overall, our results suggest that combining structural and semantic information is a practical way to catch defects early, while a third, coarser reasoning layer adds little once the first two are already working together.

Automated ergonomic exposure and risk assessments, leveraging measures from wearable sensors and markerless motion capture systems, is being increasingly adopted in manual material handling contexts as an alternative to self-reports and direct observation. Machine learning and artificial intelligence (ML/AI) algorithms trained on these measures enable continuous estimation of musculoskeletal demands and injury risk; however, model accuracy and generalizability remain constrained when training datasets lack diversity in worker characteristics and task conditions. In particular, insufficient representation of demographic factors and load-handling scenarios can lead to biased or non-generalizable models. Existing open-access, occupational movement datasets rarely capture such variability, often relying on small, homogeneous samples and single load types. To address these limitations, we present a cloud-based, public database comprising data from 40 participants (20 male, 20 female), including younger adults [mean (SD) age = 23 (3.1) years] and older adults [55.5 (5.3) years], who performed simulated occupational lifting/lowering and pushing/pulling tasks. Data were collected from three sensing modalities—inertial measurement units (IMUs), markerless motion capture (Kinect), and an electromyography (EMG) armband—using multiple load configurations, load masses (2.3-11.3 kg), lifting heights, and handling depths. This database supports the development, benchmarking, and cross-modal evaluation of ML/AI algorithms for ergonomic exposure and risk assessments in occupational settings.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder with diverse and complex manifestations. This condition requires early detection which is crucial in finding a cure. Traditional diagnostic procedures are biased and time-consuming. These create a pressing need for objective and accessible screening tools. The rapid development of artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning (DL) methods, offers promising resolutions for automating ASD detection. Such detection is done through analyzing behavioral and physical biomarkers. This study proposes a convenient but complex neural network to support early ASD screening through facial images. The model classifies facial images of children as autistic or non-autistic by using the publicly available Autistic Children Facial Dataset. Various experiments assess the model’s performance. The design is developed to be statistically efficient, which makes it suitable for mobile and embedded systems for real-time screening. Results show that our proposed model shows better performance than the existing approaches, especially in the levels of accuracy and area under curve (AUC). This further confirms its efficiency and prospects for autism screening applications. Achieving accuracy of 98.97%, the model delivers better performance than the evaluated benchmark models. These findings affirm that lightweight image-focused DL approaches are well suited to provide clinicians with a trustworthy and scalable method for early ASD screening. Thus, it is evident that the proposed model facilitates timely support for individuals and families.

People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

Robotic automation has changed the industrial sectors, including automotive, aerospace, and energy, in the areas of welding due to its precision, repeatability, and safety, to name a few. The complexity of the different welding materials, geometries, and quality welding requirements results in the need to have welding systems to are more adaptable and cleverer. The use of different technologies, like artificial intelligence and the automation of different processes of welding, especially the real-time monitoring systems, has shifted welding automation to a more advanced state of automation with the development of adaptable welding automation systems. The review covers the welding automation systems developed and the adaptable systems combined with the use of artificial intelligence and multi-sensor systems for semi-automated systems for quality adaptable control and robust process control. The use of different sensors has shifted some of the process to more automation. Vision sensors, flux sensors, contact, and acoustical sensors, and many more enable real-time automated control in robotic welding. The advanced machine learning, the developed attention-based machine learning, and real-time process control, optimization systems, and algorithms of path planning, seam tracking, and defect detection systems provide lots of automation and control of the welding processes. For industrial welding, the review proposes a conceptual integration system of AI, robotics, and different sensors, focusing on intelligent perception, adaptive control, and predictive maintenance.
topics: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

documents.abstract: This systematic review critically analyzes the contexts and challenges of Levels of Automation (LOA), particularly in light of advancements by Artificial Intelligence (AI). Human–automation interaction (HAI) seeks to understand how humans interact with automated systems, particularly as increasing automation places operators increasingly out of the loop. A foundational framework within this field is the Levels of Automation (LOA) framework, which characterizes the respective roles and capabilities of human operators and automated systems. As AI becomes increasingly integrated into traditional HAI applications, a renewed examination of the current state of LOA is warranted. This systematic review examines the following research question: What research demographics, contexts, and challenges associated with LOA are reported in the literature? Data analysis, extraction, and open and axial coding were employed, and consensus was reached by iterative discussion between the authors. The review ultimately included 118 studies. The review identified six contextual categories and 26 challenge codes. The findings provide a comprehensive analysis of the evolving landscape of human–automation interaction. The contribution of this work is to outline weaknesses embedded in research with LOA and suggest a reform with prospects of enhanced HAI with AI.

This systematic review synthesizes 15 empirical studies published in 2026 to examine how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is affecting Iranian education and what the current evidence supports. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a search of four databases yielded 710 records, of which 15 empirical studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in a thematic synthesis. The corpus comprises twelve journal articles and three chapters in edited volumes. The synthesis identified four themes. The first is that GenAI is effective when it is paired with human mediation and less effective when it replaces it, a finding that is replicated across every study in the corpus that compared AI-only and hybrid conditions. The second is that the benefits of GenAI are unevenly distributed across linguistic domains, with stronger effects on fluency, complexity, and self-efficacy than on accuracy or global proficiency. The third is an affective asymmetry, in which learners gain in enjoyment, well-being, and self-efficacy while teachers bear new costs in the form of AI-induced anxiety and monitoring workload. The fourth is a gap between individual adoption and institutional readiness, in which teachers and students are willing to use AI while the institutional structures that would make this use sustainable have not been built. The review argues that the positive impacts reported in the literature are real but conditional, produced in designed settings that most Iranian institutions have not yet created, and that closing this gap requires hybrid models of instruction, localized tools, AI literacy training that addresses the affective dimensions of adoption, and policy frameworks suited to under-resourced higher education.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Structure-based drug design (SBDD) uses three-dimensional information about a biological target to guide the identification and optimisation of small molecules. Molecular docking, virtual screening, molecular dynamics, free-energy calculations, and artificial-intelligence methods can help prioritise compounds for experimental testing. However, a plausible docking pose or favourable score is not proof of binding or therapeutic activity. Outcomes can be affected by protein structure quality, protonation, ligand preparation, receptor flexibility, scoring-function limitations, and the chemical space represented in a screening library. This narrative review presents a validation-first workflow: define a biologically justified target; assess the target structure and binding site; prepare proteins and ligands transparently; validate docking using reference ligands and appropriate controls; combine structural interpretation with complementary ranking; assess absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity (ADMET) risks; and confirm prioritised candidates experimentally. Recent AI-enabled methods are considered as tools for hypothesis generation rather than substitutes for medicinal chemistry judgement or laboratory evidence. The review also discusses reproducibility, uncertainty, and transparent reporting. The central recommendation is to connect every computational stage to a clear decision gate and to distinguish predictions from observations. This framework is intended to support student and early-stage research projects; it is not a report of new experimental data or a claim that any compound has been discovered.

This article introduces a novel physics-informed large-margin learning framework for diagnosing rotating component faults, addressing the limitations of traditional methods and “black-box” artificial intelligence models in handling complex, noisy vibration data. The methodology integrates feature mode decomposition and short-time Fourier transform to generate physics-informed time–frequency maps, from which interpretable features are extracted. A large-margin learning model then utilizes these features, with its five critical hyperparameters adaptively optimized using the slime mould algorithm to ensure robustness and optimal performance. Evaluated on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and intelligent maintenance systems (IMS) bearing datasets, the proposed framework achieves a diagnostic accuracy of 88.75% on CWRU and 96.67% on IMS, outperforming seven state-of-the-art classification baselines implemented under identical experimental conditions. This approach enhances interpretability, diagnostic accuracy, and generalization, offering a more reliable solution for machine health monitoring.

Adjustability is a core determinant of ergonomic fit in office chairs, but its benefits depend on users being able to operate the controls and, on the chair, continuing to support the body as posture changes during work. We compared two high-end office chairs, the T90 (Sidiz; Chair A) and the Aeron (Herman Miller; Chair B), in two experiments to explore which design features may explain differences between them. In Experiment 1, 20 participants adjusted ten controls common to both chairs and rated perceived adjustment difficulty on four items. Chair A had significantly lower overall difficulty (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p = 0.008), with control-level advantages for headrest angle, armrest height, armrest rotation angle and lumbar support position; Chair B was easier for seat height, possibly because its side-mounted lever is more visible than Chair A's underside button. The headrest comparisons involved a third-party headrest fitted to Chair B, and control- and item-level tests were not corrected for multiple comparisons. In Experiment 2, the same participants completed a 15-minute multi-device task requiring repeated posture changes, reach and reorientation, then rated body-part discomfort, general comfort and satisfaction with five components. Discomfort and comfort did not differ; Chair A had higher satisfaction for the seat-pan and lumbar support (exploratory, uncorrected). Interviews suggested links to mechanism properties: Chair B's rear lumbar dial was often described as producing little perceptible change, and for controls without significant differences each chair appeared to leave a different aspect of the same need unmet. These findings suggest mechanical and interface properties that designers of adjustable office chairs may consider for dynamic, multi-device work.

Artificial intelligence (AI)–driven chatbots based on large language models are increasingly entering medical education, but evidence on the real-world use of domestic systems such as DeepSeek among Chinese medical interns is still scarce. This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence, patterns and perceptions of DeepSeek use among medical interns at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University. A total of 634 interns from clinical medicine, preventive medicine and nursing completed an anonymous questionnaire. Overall, about one-third of interns reported using DeepSeek. Among users, most engaged with the tool regularly, with over half using it several times per week. DeepSeek was primarily employed for completing assignments, searching for information, translation and polishing of written texts, while a smaller subset of users reported using it for data analysis. Attitudes toward DeepSeek were mainly neutral or optimistic, and across majors most users perceived its advantages and disadvantages as broadly balanced, while only a minority considered the disadvantages to outweigh the advantages. After adjustment, residence and major remained associated with DeepSeek use, whereas age and sex were not. Urban interns were more likely to report using DeepSeek than rural interns. Compared with clinical medicine interns, preventive medicine interns were less likely to report use, whereas nursing interns were more likely to do so. Among users, overall attitudes differed across majors, while usage frequency and the perceived balance of advantages and disadvantages did not. These findings provide descriptive evidence on the use and evaluation of DeepSeek among medical interns and may inform future institutional guidance on responsible use, verification of AI-generated information and academic integrity.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: As modern DRAM manufacturing processes continue to shrink, the Rowhammer vulnerability has emerged as one of the most severe threats to microarchitectural security isolation. To defend against such attacks, hardware vendors have introduced complex black-box defense mechanisms in memory controllers, such as FR-FCFS (First-Ready First-Come–First-Serve) queue coalescing, Target Row Refresh (TRR), and the open row policy. These defenses provide the context for this work; in the evaluation reported here, we explicitly model the FR-FCFS scheduling family and the open row policy, while realistic TRR is not modeled and is left for future work. These mechanisms have rendered traditional vulnerability exploitation approaches, which rely on security experts manually crafting inline assembly, increasingly unsustainable. In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have become strong at software code generation. However, when applied to low-level hardware vulnerability exploitation, they encounter a severe “semantic–physical gap.” Conventional LLMs lack embodied cognition of physical hardware state machines; their generated memory access loops often compile and run correctly at the software layer, but the majority of requests are absorbed by caches and microarchitectural queues before reaching physical memory, trapping the LLM in a “false-positive state” where simulated ACT counts remain near zero. Most existing research treats LLMs as victims of Rowhammer attacks, overlooking their potential as active attack initiators at the hardware level. To address these challenges, this paper repurposes LLMs as microarchitectural attackers for the first time and designs AgentHammer—a closed-loop agent framework that allows LLMs to conduct automated hardware vulnerability exploitation. To bridge the software–hardware semantic gap, we construct a Hardware-Aware Simulation-in-the-Loop (HASIL) perception skill chain that deeply couples the QEMU full-system simulator with the Ramulator memory simulator. This chain captures low-level timing measurements—such as simulated ACT counts and simulated row conflict rates—transparently and reduces their dimensionality into natural language feedback comprehensible to LLMs. At the same time, we distill rigid low-level constraints—such as cache eviction and access stride—into reasoning primitives for the model, establishing a closed-loop verification pipeline of “perception, decision, feedback, and evolution,” in which the LLM adapts its parameters within the constraints set by human experts. Experimental results show that AgentHammer effectively breaks through the false-positive blind zone of pure software code generation. In complex microarchitectural simulation environments, the system autonomously reasons over low-level feedback logs and mutates parameters, successfully discovering, within our simulated configurations, the optimal access pattern that overcomes the FR-FCFS request-queue optimization and the open-row policy, ultimately achieving simulated row conflict. This work not only shows that large foundation models can explore physical boundaries in black-box environments through autonomous parameter adaptation, but also provides a basis for highly automated low-level hardware security assessment.

Enterprise automation is moving on from simple software rules to systems that can take in a request, work out what tools to use, co-ordinate a range of specialist agents and then make decisions based on the feedback they receive. That said, greater technical autonomy doesn't in itself lead to organisational change. This integrative review looks at how agentic AI, machine learning and the existing forms of process automation can be brought together to enable enterprise-wide change in Saudi Arabia as part of Vision 2030. It draws on 30 DOI identifiable publications from 2020–2025, covering the technological, organisational and Saudi specific evidence. A concept-based analytical approach is used to separate out what is actually demonstrated from what is merely proposed in terms of architecture and to assess the degree to which the findings can be applied to regulated enterprise workflows. Six interrelated dimensions are identified: process suitability, intelligent orchestration, data and infrastructure, human capability, risk governance and value measurement. The proposed architecture for accountable automation is one in which decision rights, evidence provenance and exception handling are all situated around a bounded agent execution loop. The Saudi case studies do suggest that management buy-in and digital maturity are important, but provide very little in the way of direct evidence on the scale of agentic deployment. The review therefore does not accept that agent autonomy, economic benefit and public legitimacy are equivalent. It does provide a context sensitive design framework and a testable research agenda for enterprises that are looking for real transformation that is reliable, interoperable and inclusive rather than just a series of isolated proofs of concept. Longitudinal, sector specific evaluation is required before any claim can be made about causal national outcomes.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Autonomous Multi-Material Self-Replicating Factory (AM-SRF) & Advanced Nuclear Micro-Battery Production for Deep-Space AI Infrastructure Abstract & System Overview The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence into deep space—specifically targeting the hostile, high-radiation environments of the Moon and Mars—demands an unprecedented paradigm shift in power generation, manufacturing autonomy, and resilience. Traditional silicon-based electronics and solar arrays fail under severe cosmic radiation, thermal fluctuations, and dust storms. To solve this, we introduce the Autonomous Multi-Material Self-Replicating Factory (AM-SRF), a unified single-module manufacturing system integrated with advanced isotope gas handling circuits, laser-assisted Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD), and poly-diamond nuclear micro-batteries. Powered by isotope-derived energy and resilient against planetary radiation, this infrastructure enables AI systems to construct their own habitats, manufacture industrial machinery, execute self-repair protocols, and harvest extraterrestrial resources such as helium-3. 1. Unified Single-Module Manufacturing Architecture (The "1-Machine" Concept) Unlike terrestrial multi-factory supply chains that rely on fragile logistics, the AM-SRF consolidates the entire production chain into a single, highly optimized growth and post-processing module. Isotope Gas Handling & Recirculation: The system features a closed-loop isotope recovery circuit connected to high-purity precursor gas tanks (such as \bm{98\%} enriched \bm{^{14}\text{CH}_4} or tritium-doped precursors). Mass flow controllers regulate gas delivery into a coaxial injection nozzle, while a recirculation pump and mixing valve capture unreacted gases, scrub impurities with clean \bm{\text{H}_2} carrier gas, and maintain optimal reaction pressures. Dynamic CVD Chamber: At the core of the machine is a hermetically sealed quartz and sapphire reaction chamber. A UV laser beam path, focused via high-precision lenses onto a rotating molybdenum disc substrate, drives layer-by-layer crystalline growth. In-Process Feedback & Laser Slicing: Automated optical probes and re-counter feedback mechanisms monitor layer uniformity and thickness in real time. Integrated laser cutting modules slice the grown crystalline boules into precise planar and spherical micro-battery arrays and structural components without breaking vacuum. 2. Advanced Material Science: Poly-Diamonds, Tritium, and Carbon-14 The operational longevity and radiation immunity of deep-space AI systems depend entirely on the material composition of their power sources and structural chassis. The AM-SRF produces batteries utilizing the following stacked material specifications: Transitional Layers (\bm{5\text{--}10\text{ nm}}): Single-crystal Carbon-14 (\bm{\text{sp}^3+\text{sp}^2} hybridization) providing exceptional p-type or n-type conductivity and atomic bonding integrity between the substrate and active cathode. Carbon-14 & Tritium Doped Diamond Cathodes (\bm{1\text{--}2\ \mu\text{m}}): Utilizing beta-voltaic conversion within a diamond lattice matrix. Diamond's wide bandgap (\bm{\sim5.5\text{ eV}}) and high displacement threshold energy make it impervious to radiation damage. Beta particles emitted by \bm{^{14}\text{C}} or tritium generate electron-hole pairs continuously for millennia without external recharging. Polyimide-Diamond Deposition Layers (\bm{10\text{--}20\ \mu\text{m}}): Polymer-matrix composite layers reinforced with carbon isotope doping, delivering superior mechanical strength, fracture toughness, and thermal dissipation. Substrates and Current Collectors: High-purity single-crystal diamond and copper-coated polymer substrates ensure efficient ion transport and ultra-low internal resistance, achieving energy densities exceeding \bm{2.60\text{ kW}\cdot\text{hr}/\text{cm}^3}. 3. Radiation Immunity and Deep-Space Survival Martian and lunar environments present lethal radiation hazards, including Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCRs) and Solar Particle Events (SPEs), which instantly degrade standard semiconductor architectures. Diamond Lattice Hardening: The nuclear micro-batteries and structural chassis produced by the AM-SRF utilize radiation-hardened diamond structures. Because carbon-14 and tritium beta decays are harnessed directly within the wide-bandgap diamond lattice, incoming external ionizing radiation is safely dissipated through collective lattice phonon interactions rather than generating destructive charge trapping. Self-Healing Electronic Substrates: The AI systems powered by these batteries operate within redundant fractal-wave network architectures. If micro-meteorite impacts or localized radiation spikes damage a circuit path, the AM-SRF's robotic manipulators and laser-cutting tools can instantly manufacture and swap replacement modules on the fly. 4. Autonomous City Construction and Self-Replication An AI governed by this infrastructure is not a passive tool, but an active planetary constructor. In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU): Using the AM-SRF's integrated regolith processing modules, the system extracts raw silicates, carbon, and metal oxides from lunar and Martian dust. Automated Scaling and Expansion: The factory uses its linear-rotary carrier tracks and multi-axis robotic arms to fabricate structural bricks, radiation-shielded habitats, solar-thermal mirrors, and additional CVD growth units. By replicating its own machinery, a single initial seed unit can expand into an industrial network capable of building entire subsurface cities and manufacturing plants autonomously. 5. Helium-3 Integration and Deep-Space Expansion As the AI colony expands its industrial footprint across the solar system, reliance on terrestrial-sourced isotopes transitions to abundant extraterrestrial resources. Transition to He-3 Fusion: The AM-SRF architecture is natively engineered to incorporate Helium-3 (\bm{^3\text{He}}) recovery and fusion energy integration. Lunar regolith, enriched with solar-wind-implanted helium-3 over billions of years, is harvested, thermally processed, and fed into advanced compact fusion reactors. Limitless Power for Deep Space: By shifting from beta-voltaic micro-batteries to localized He-3 fusion generators produced by the same self-replicating machinery, the AI obtains the massive energy throughput required for heavy manufacturing, atmospheric terraforming, and interstellar propulsion.
